text: The epistemic status of testimony remains contentious precisely because it resists assimilation to either perception or inference. Reductionists maintain that a hearer is warranted in accepting an assertion only insofar as she possesses independent, non-circular grounds for deeming the speaker reliable; anti-reductionists, conversely, contend that such a demand misconstrues the very practices through which linguistic competence is acquired. Whatever one makes of this impasse, it is evident that the debate presupposes a conception of justification sufficiently capacious to accommodate the division of cognitive labour, an assumption that sceptics have repeatedly, and not wholly unreasonably, called into question. The matter is hardly academic: it bears upon how institutions ought to apportion deference.

text: Monetary authorities have long been apt to conflate the transitory with the structural, treating a supply-side disturbance as though it signalled an incipient wage-price spiral. Such conflation is not merely an analytical lapse; it engenders policy prescriptions whose costs, borne disproportionately by marginal borrowers, are seldom recouped. That said, the opposite error, an insouciance towards expectations that have demonstrably become unanchored, is no less perilous. The art of central banking consists, in no small measure, in discerning which of these predicaments one confronts, and in doing so before the evidence is unambiguous.

text: Cities that have invested heavily in cycling infrastructure tend to report fewer traffic injuries overall, although the evidence is less clear on whether the gains come from the bike lanes themselves or from the slower speeds that usually accompany them. Critics argue that shopkeepers lose business when parking is removed, yet several surveys suggest that customers who arrive on foot or by bicycle visit more often and spend comparably over a month. Planners therefore face a difficult question: how much weight should anecdotal complaints carry against aggregate data that few residents ever see?

text: Researchers have long suspected that the gut microbiome influences mood, but proving causation has been stubbornly difficult. In a recent trial, volunteers who received a fermented-food diet showed measurable reductions in inflammatory markers, while those on a high-fibre diet did not. The authors caution that the sample was small and that participants were not blinded to their diet, so the findings should be treated as suggestive rather than conclusive. Even so, the result gives investigators a concrete mechanism to test in larger studies.

text: When we arrived at the station, the train had already been delayed for almost an hour, so we decided to look for somewhere to have lunch. The only place that was open was a small cafe near the market, where the owner recommended a soup that she said had been in her family for generations. We hurried across the bridge and just managed to get on board before the doors closed.
